Export and redraw figures

plot-export.Rmd

A figure needs to remain useful after you close the plotting session. Choose the format according to what you want to do next. Use PDF or SVG for a scalable static figure, HTML for exploration, and RDS when you want to return to the same object and change its appearance.

Saving a plot and saving an analysis are different tasks. Keep your fitted result lists, input data and contrast settings as well as the exported picture. A PNG is convenient to share, but it cannot tell you all the choices that produced it.

Current export interfaces

Table 1. Figure export formats
Figure object Saving interface
PCA, heatmap, error-bar, contribution boxplot, dendrogram and effect ggplots ggplot2::ggsave()
Taxonomy/phylogeny Sankey save_sankey(); HTML, SVG, PDF, PNG and RDS
Ordinary Sankey (tree_mode = "none") save_sankey(); HTML or RDS
Chord save_chord(); HTML, SVG, PDF, PNG and RDS

Use ggsave() for the returned ggplots, and the dedicated save_sankey() or save_chord() functions for those diagram objects.

Sankey

Tree-enabled Sankey diagrams keep a fixed layout across their HTML and static exports. This is useful when you want to explore a relationship interactively and then present the same geometry in a report. For a very tall diagram, decide whether one fitted page or continuation pages will make the labels easier to read.

save_sankey(p_tax_sankey, file.path(out, "sankey.html"))
save_sankey(p_tax_sankey, file.path(out, "sankey.svg"))
save_sankey(p_tax_sankey, file.path(out, "sankey.pdf"))
save_sankey(p_tax_sankey, file.path(out, "sankey.png"), width = 1800)
save_sankey(p_tax_sankey, file.path(out, "sankey.rds"))

p_redrawn <- redraw_sankey(
  file.path(out, "sankey.rds"), tree_options = list(font_size = 16)
)
save_sankey(p_redrawn, file.path(out, "sankey_redrawn.html"))

Tree PNG/PDF export requires rsvg. For very large tree diagrams, pdf_mode = "tiles" writes vertical continuation pages and requires qpdf; labels or ribbons can cross page boundaries. RDS keeps the original result and tree for redrawing without recomputing the statistical analysis.

p_plain <- tax2fun_sankey(result_taxa, tree_mode = "none")
save_sankey(p_plain, file.path(out, "sankey_no_tree.html"), selfcontained = FALSE)

Keep the adjacent dependency folder with ordinary HTML exports when selfcontained = FALSE. A self-contained ordinary HTML export requires Pandoc. Static SVG/PDF/PNG exports require a tree mode.

Chord

A Chord can contain more labels than comfortably fit around its circle. Export the label mapping and legends with the graphic so that compact labels remain interpretable. The interactive HTML is useful for finding a sector; the static PDF is useful when you want a figure and its complete legend in a document.

save_chord(p_tax_chord, file.path(out, "chord.html"))
save_chord(p_tax_chord, file.path(out, "chord.pdf"), width = 12, height = 11)
save_chord(p_tax_chord, file.path(out, "chord.png"))
save_chord(p_tax_chord, file.path(out, "chord.rds"))

# The explicit extension is included along with the additional formats.
save_chord(p_tax_chord, file.path(out, "chord.html"), formats = c("pdf", "png"))

Chord HTML includes zoom controls and a searchable sector legend. Selecting a legend entry highlights its sector; select it again or press Escape to clear. Labels that do not fit can be omitted from the graphic. The mapping CSV retains all labels and their visible status. Static legends may continue on separate PDF pages or companion files.

ggplot figures 

ggplot2::ggsave(file.path(out, "boxplot.pdf"), p_tax_box,
                width = 10, height = 6)

Create the objects first using the taxon-to-function or function-to-taxon plotting examples.
